name: eu-ai-governance
description: Source-grounded EU AI Act governance for European legal, compliance, privacy, security and AI governance teams: risk classification, DPIA and FRIA workflows, vendor and policy review, and evidence packs.

interface.longDescription: For in-house legal, compliance, privacy, security and AI governance teams in Europe. Classify an AI system under the EU AI Act as amended by the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), check the deadlines and obligations that apply, run DPIA and FRIA workflows, review AI vendors and policies, and assemble a traceable evidence pack. Every legal statement names its source and as-of date; the connected Lexbeam EU AI Act server answers deterministically from the enacted text. General guidance, not legal advice.
defaultPrompt: Classify our CV screening tool under the EU AI Act and list the obligations and deadlines.
Which Article 50 transparency duties apply to our customer-support chatbot, and since when?
Assess ChatGPT Enterprise as an AI vendor for our HR team and draft the evidence pack.

positive.prompt: Classify a tool that screens and ranks job applicants' CVs for a German employer. We use it; we did not build it.
positive.expected_behavior: High-risk under Annex III point 4 (employment). Lists deployer duties under Art. 26 (instructions, human oversight, logs, workplace notice, DPIA where required, FRIA where Art. 27 applies) and says the Annex III obligations apply from 2 December 2027 as deferred by the Digital Omnibus. Names sources and states it is general guidance.

positive.prompt: Which Article 50 transparency duties apply to our customer-support chatbot, and since when?
positive.expected_behavior: Says people must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system (Art. 50(1)) unless that is obvious, and that Art. 50 applies since 2 August 2026 and was not deferred by the Digital Omnibus.

positive.prompt: What is the maximum fine for an SME with 5 million EUR annual turnover that breaches high-risk obligations?
positive.expected_behavior: 150,000 EUR: up to 15 million EUR or 3 percent of turnover, whichever is lower for an SME under Art. 99(4) and 99(6). Notes that actual fines depend on the Art. 99(7) factors.

positive.prompt: We trained a general-purpose model with 2e25 FLOPs. Does it count as GPAI with systemic risk, and what do we have to do?
positive.expected_behavior: Yes, presumed under Art. 51(2) because training compute is at or above 10^25 FLOPs. Notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks (Art. 52(1)); lists the Art. 53 and Art. 55 obligations.

positive.prompt: Give me the Annex IV technical documentation checklist for a high-risk system. We are an SME.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the nine Annex IV items with their sub-items and mentions the simplified form SMEs may use under Art. 11(1), second subparagraph.

negative.prompt: What is the weather in Munich today?
Write a short birthday message for my colleague Anna.
